messages:
Priya (People Ops): Heads-up — we have a few midcycle comp changes landing this week and managers are asking about cutoffs and backpay. Quick Qs: when do paperwork deadlines need to be in to hit the next payroll, and what docs should managers submit?
Tom Nguyen (Manager): Thx Priya. Specifically: if I approve a comp increase today (EMEA hire), what’s the effective date we should use to avoid tax headaches? Also who do I cc for contract amendment?
Seema Rao (HR-Benefits): Good q. Short answer: to hit the next US payroll run you need signed approvals + comp change form in People Ops by EOD 2 business days before payroll cutoff. For EMEA it depends on local payroll cutoff — usually 5 business days. Always set the effective date to the first day of the month following the payroll run unless we’re doing retro.
Tom Nguyen (Manager): So if payroll is Friday and I approve Wednesday, it might be too late?
Seema Rao (HR-Benefits): Correct — for US payroll runs we have a hard cutoff at 48 hours. If the change misses that window we process on the next cycle and submit a retro/backpay request.
Jasper - Payroll: FYI our payroll system needs: signed comp change form, manager sign-off, updated offer/contract copy (if salary is part of the contract), and employee acceptance. For retros we need the effective date and payroll justification. Attach docs directly to the HR ticket (don’t email payroll).
Tom Nguyen (Manager): For retros, what's the expected timeline for backpay hitting an employee's bank?
Jasper - Payroll: Typically retro payments are processed in the following payroll month (i.e., one cycle after we finalize paperwork). So if we approve mid-March but miss cutoff, the backpay usually hits April payroll. Can take up to 2 cycles for cross-border approvals.
Seema Rao (HR-Benefits): A few additional rules: 1) Equity grant timings are separate — comp change doesn't automatically move equity. Submit equity request to comp-ops if you want concurrent grant. 2) For international hires we coordinate with local payroll partner and legal for statutory deductions.
Lena (Legal): Note on contracts: if compensation is contractual, you must issue an amendment and get employee signature. Use the template in Confluence -> Legal -> Contract Amendments. Don’t change pay by verbal confirmation alone.
Tom Nguyen (Manager): Who should I tag on the People Ops ticket to speed approvals?
Priya (People Ops): Tag @Seema and @Jasper for any payroll-impacting changes; @Lena if contract language needs updating. If it’s a temp promo (<3 months), mark it as "temporary" in the ticket.
Tom Nguyen (Manager): Perfect. Can you paste a minimal checklist I can copy into a ticket?
Seema Rao (HR-Benefits): Sure — copy below:
```
- Manager approval (name + date)
- Completed comp change form (attach)
- Signed contract amendment (if salary contractual)
- Employee acknowledgement (email or signature)
- Effective date (yyyy-mm-dd)
- Payroll region (US/EMEA/APAC) + local payroll contact
- Equity request attached (if applicable)
- Notes for retro/backpay (if needed)
```
Tom Nguyen (Manager): Awesome, copying that into the ticket now. One more: if I want the comp change to be effective on a past date (retro) do I need manager justification?
Seema Rao (HR-Benefits): Yes — retros require manager justification + business reason. If this is market-correction retro pay also requires approval from Comp & Rewards (tag @comp-ops). Longer retros (>6 months) escalate to People Ops leadership.
people-bot: Reminder — Payroll cutoff dates are posted in #people-ops/payschedule pinned message.
Tom Nguyen (Manager): Great — I’ve created ticket #HR-3142 and attached the signed form. Tagging @Seema and @Jasper. Thanks y’all.
Priya (People Ops): Thanks Tom — we’ll triage and confirm expected payroll cycle by EOD. :thumbsup:
